methodological_rigor.justification: The retrospective phase is methodologically strong: a prespecified 5% noninferiority margin, a power calculation targeting 80% at the site level (~25,000 women/site, 200 cancers/site), a rigorous 39-month ground truth capturing interval and next-round cancers, and stratified sampling across five NHS services with diverse workflows and vendors. Statistical analyses are appropriate: one-sided testing at 0.025, Holm-Bonferroni correction for primary endpoints, Wald/Obuchowski-McNemar for clustered paired binary data, Wald CIs with bootstrap fallback for small cells, and 10,000-iteration bootstrapping for breast/lesion-level inference. Weaknesses: analyses were explicitly not blinded; interval cancers were enriched to match SHIM-reported rates, which may bias prevalence estimates; women without follow-up were replaced by matched women with follow-up (acknowledged exclusion of possibly underserved populations); multiplicity was not corrected for secondary/exploratory subgroup analyses; and service-specific OP tuning risks optimistic site-level performance. The prospective phase is appropriately framed as a technical feasibility study (not powered for accuracy) and candidly exposes distribution-shift challenges.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The design is an individual multicenter diagnostic cohort study with ISRCTN registration (60839016, 88754382) and ethics approval, plus a prospective non-interventional feasibility deployment at 12 sites; neither phase is randomized, placing the work at Oxford LoE 2b. Clinical relevance is high: endpoints (sensitivity, specificity, CDR, interval cancer detection, recall rate, reader-time burden) are directly operational for a national breast screening program, the AI is evaluated against the actual NHS double-reader workflow it would replace, and the 25.0% capture of future interval cancers suggests meaningful early-diagnosis potential. The translational path is explicit (replacement of a second reader with iterative OP calibration), and findings directly inform NHS BSP guidance, though the work does not demonstrate downstream patient outcomes (mortality, QoL) and the companion workflow trial is cited for arbitration/interaction impact.

reporting_quality.justification: STARD is the applicable standard given the diagnostic-accuracy focus (test characteristics vs clinical reference standard); REMARK/TRIPOD are tangential here. The paper reports prespecified primary and secondary endpoints, inclusion/exclusion criteria, ground-truth definition with time window, reader comparators, operating-point selection methodology, statistical plan, and flow diagrams in Extended Data Fig. 1; ethics approvals and trial registration are explicit. Minor omissions: no explicit STARD checklist, limited reporting of indeterminate results and of time-interval between index test and reference standard variability; blinding of index/reference test was not performed. Data availability is partial: Source Data for figures and tables are indicated and OPTIMAM is referenced for underlying mammograms, but there is no analytical code deposit mentioned and raw patient-level data are governed by NHS data access.

novelty_literature.justification: The AI system (Google v1.2) is an iteration of the previously published v1.0 (McKinney 2020), so this is not a first-in-class model; comparable large AI-independent-reader evaluations exist (MASAI/Lang 2023, Lauritzen 2024, Dembrower 2023, Sharma 2023). Genuine novelty lies in the empirical dimension: largest UK NHS multi-service retrospective validation with 39-month ground truth including interval and next-round cancers; prospective silent feasibility deployment demonstrating a quantified distribution shift between 2016 tuning data and 2023 deployment; and formal fairness/subgroup analyses with calibration curves across ethnicity, IMD, density, and device. Methodological novelty is modest (operating-point adaptive calibration workflow, breast- and lesion-level IoU evaluation with radiologist review). Overall an important incremental extension rather than paradigm-shifting.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is clearly written and logically organized: the abstract is quantitatively grounded (sensitivities, specificities, CDR, reader-time reductions) and faithful to the results; sections follow a clean design-methods-results-discussion arc; figure captions are informative and standalone (Fig. 2 explicitly states tests used and n per level). Discussion engages limitations substantively (subgroup sample sizes, drift, excluded underserved women, lack of outcomes data) rather than merely listing them. Minor issues: dense methodological prose in the Methods section, some redundancy between Discussion and Results on subgroup findings, and heavy reliance on Supplementary Notes/Extended Data for critical details (OP selection, curation).

key_strengths: Large multi-center retrospective evaluation (115,973 women across 5 NHS services, three workflows) with a rigorous 39-month ground truth that captures interval and next-round cancers
Prespecified noninferiority design with power calculation, Holm-Bonferroni correction, and appropriate clustered paired tests (Obuchowski-McNemar) and bootstrapping for small subgroups
Superior sensitivity (0.541 vs 0.437) with noninferior specificity vs first reader, and detection of 25% of interval cancers; especially strong performance on prevalent screens and invasive cancers
Prospective silent feasibility deployment at 12 sites that candidly quantifies real-world distribution shift and demonstrates an iterative OP recalibration workflow
Fairness analyses across ethnicity, IMD, breast density, age, and device vendor with calibration curves and transparent reporting of borderline subgroups
key_concerns: Analyses were explicitly not blinded; replacement of women lacking follow-up and enrichment of interval cancers to match SHIM rates introduce potential selection and prevalence bias that is acknowledged but not quantified via sensitivity analysis

Per-site operating-point tuning risks site-optimized performance; the 2023 prospective phase required threshold recalibration after 2 weeks, raising questions about generalizability of the reported retrospective gains
Several subgroup conclusions (mixed ethnicity, IMD decile 1) are underpowered with wide CIs; multiplicity was not controlled for secondary/exploratory endpoints
No deposited analytical code and raw mammography data remain access-controlled, limiting independent reproducibility beyond Source Data for figures
Downstream clinical and economic outcomes (mortality, assessment-clinic burden under real deployment) are not measured and are deferred to companion/future interventional studies
chief_reviewer.rationale: Rigorous, large-scale, pre-registered multicenter validation of a breast-screening AI with a transparent prospective feasibility component and candid treatment of distribution shift and fairness places this at tier 1 (Lancet Oncology / Lancet Digital Health / Nature Medicine class), contingent on minor revisions clarifying selection-bias sensitivity analyses, OP-tuning generalizability, and reproducibility materials.
